heading: The Okanagan in November, 2026
title: The Okanagan in November 2026 | Okanagan Roam
description: Things to do in the Okanagan in November 2026: shows, first light-ups, quiet-season wine, saunas, soup and ramen, and ski hills opening late in the month.
intro: November is the in-between month in the Okanagan. The harvest is in, the summer crowds are long gone, and the ski hills are getting ready to open. It's a quiet, easy time to visit: tasting rooms are calm, the arts season is in full swing, and the first holiday lights go on near the end of the month.

This guide picks a handful of November events, then adds quiet-season wine, indoor warm-ups, cozy food and the start of ski season. For every dated event, see {page:/whats-on|What's On}. For the holidays, see our {page:/guides/okanagan-holiday-events|holiday events guide} and our {page:/guides/okanagan-christmas-markets|Christmas markets guide}.

sections.heading: On the calendar in November
sections.lead: A few of the month's strongest dates, from festivals to dance and music.

items.name: 2026 Okanagan Mushroom Festival
items.text: artisans, crafters, growers and mushroom fans at the Westbank Lions Community Centre from 11 am. Entry is by donation, with proceeds going to Stars Piggly Wiggly Animal Sanctuary.

items.name: Penticton Farmers’ Market 2026
items.text: 90+ stalls of South Okanagan produce, honey, baking and preserves. In November and December the market moves indoors to Cherry Lane Mall.

items.name: Ballet Kelowna: Four Voices
items.text: the season opener at Kelowna Community Theatre, a mixed program of four works including Acts of Remembrance, which honours Canadians who served in the First World War, and two world premieres. There are 150 pay-what-you-wish seats per show.

items.name: Miigis – Red Sky Performance (Vernon)
items.text: a contemporary Indigenous dance work inspired by the Anishinaabe journey along ancient water routes, at 2 pm at the Vernon & District Performing Arts Centre. It runs under an hour.

items.name: Remembrance Day Ceremony, West Kelowna
items.text: the Royal Canadian Legion Branch 288 service, held indoors at Royal LePage Place. Be seated by 10:30; the service begins at 10:45.

items.name: Jan Lisiecki, piano – Chamber Music Kelowna
items.text: a solo recital at the Rotary Centre for the Arts at 7:30 pm. One of the season's biggest classical draws, so seats are scarce.

sections.heading: The first lights of the season
sections.lead: The holidays start in the last two weeks of November. Here are a few of the first light-ups; the full list is in our {page:/guides/okanagan-holiday-events|holiday events guide} and {page:/guides/okanagan-christmas-markets|Christmas markets guide}.

items.name: Village Light-Up at District Wine Village
items.text: live music, free skating on the outdoor rink, s'mores by the fire and winery tastings from 3 pm, with the lights on at 5 pm. Bring a food-bank donation for a free tasting.

items.name: Frostival: Downtown Vernon Winter Street Festival
items.text: four blocks of 30th Avenue close for a free street festival from 4 pm, with live music, vendors and food trucks. Parking meters are free for the day.

items.name: Downtown Kelowna Winter Street Market & Light Up
items.text: a free afternoon of vendors, family activities and stage shows in Stuart Park from noon, then the park's lights go on at 5 pm. Hot chocolate sales and donations go to the Central Okanagan Food Bank.

sections.heading: Quiet-season wine
sections.lead: November is a calm month on the wine trails. Many wineries cut their hours from November to April, so check each listing's hours before you set out. The wineries below show regular hours on their pages, and two wine weekends add some holiday cheer. Browse more on our {page:/wineries|wineries page}.

items.name: Naramata Bench Winterfest
items.text: Naramata Bench wineries and neighbours open their doors for a festive weekend of holiday tastings, treats and shopping. You hop between participating tasting rooms.

items.name: Wineries for the Holidays on the Scenic Sip Trail
items.text: from 11 am, 50th Parallel, Intrigue, Ex Nihilo and Gray Monk each host their own festive experience, from holiday markets to fire pits and food-and-wine pairings. Pay per stop.

items.name: Summerhill Pyramid Winery
items.text: a certified-organic estate built around an actual pyramid. The on-site restaurant has a heated lake-view terrace.

items.name: Quails' Gate Winery
items.text: family-farmed since 1956, with a dog-friendly patio over Okanagan Lake.

items.name: Red Rooster Winery
items.text: a Naramata Bench winery with a wide-ranging wine list and unpushy tasting staff. From fall to spring the wine shop is open Friday to Sunday.

items.name: Hester Creek Estate Winery
items.text: a winery with a patio restaurant. Reviewers rave about the gnocchi and the Golden Mile reds.

items.name: Nk'Mip Cellars
items.text: North America's first Indigenous-owned winery, with a restaurant terrace over the desert and lake.

sections.heading: Warm up indoors
sections.lead: November can be grey and damp. Head inside for heat, art and local history. Our {page:/guides/okanagan-saunas-spas|saunas & spas guide} and {page:/guides/rainy-day-okanagan|rainy-day guide} have more.

items.name: Tality Wellness Kelowna
items.text: a downtown social bathhouse with a 20-person cedar sauna, four cold plunges and a lounge around a vapour firepit. Robes, towels, kombucha and hot tea are included. Book a shared or private session.

items.name: Cleopatra's Rituals Thermal Spa and Steam
items.text: a hot-cold circuit of sauna, steam, thermal showers and a falling-snow room. There are no walk-ins, so book ahead.

items.name: Shelter Floating Sauna
items.text: a cedar sauna floating at the Lakeside Resort marina, where you cycle between heat, a cold plunge in the lake and rest. Sessions last 70 minutes and are booked online.

items.name: Sncewips Heritage Museum
items.text: Westbank First Nation's living museum, sharing syilx history, language and present-day cultural practice. Drop in by donation, or pre-book a guided tour.

items.name: Okanagan Wine & Orchard Museum (Laurel Packinghouse)
items.text: the valley's fruit and wine story, told in the historic 1918 Laurel Packinghouse. Admission is by donation, and it's a good primer before a winery day.

items.name: Briar Craig: Conversations at the Penticton Art Gallery
items.text: a solo show of layered screen prints that play with words and images, filling the gallery's Okanagan and Skaha rooms.

items.name: Vernon Public Art Gallery
items.text: the largest public art gallery in the North Okanagan, with changing contemporary exhibitions and admission by donation. An easy, low-cost stop on a grey afternoon.

sections.heading: Cozy food
sections.lead: Soup, ramen and warm dining rooms for short, cool days. Our {page:/guides/cozy-spots-okanagan|cozy spots guide} has more.

items.name: Bon Ga Korean Cuisine
items.text: a family-owned kitchen. Build your order around the hot bone soup, especially on a cold day.

items.name: Mad Mango Cafe
items.text: a cozy, colourful pan-Asian soup spot on Bernard Ave. Order the laksa.

items.name: Two Brothers Mexican Restaurant
items.text: a small, cozy Mexican spot. The pozole is the dish that keeps regulars coming back.

items.name: BRODO Kitchen
items.text: a lunch-only soup and sandwich spot. Order the soup and sandwich combo.

items.name: Theo's Restaurant
items.text: a traditional Greek dining room with timber beams and a wood-smoke atmosphere. Plant-based diners can order the vegan moussaka.

items.name: Raku Rice & Noodle Bar
items.text: widely called the best ramen in Vernon. Dine in or take it home.

items.name: Farmhouse Cafe
items.text: a café that grows what it cooks on site. Order the soup and sandwich, and add a fresh-baked scone.

sections.heading: Ski season is coming
sections.lead: The hills open near the end of the month. Our {page:/guides/ski-season-big-white-silverstar|ski season guide to Big White and SilverStar} covers lifts, lessons and where to eat on the mountain.

items.name: Warren Miller's Days Off
items.text: the Big White Ski Club screens the latest Warren Miller ski and snowboard film at the Rotary Centre for the Arts at 6:30 pm. A classic way to kick off ski season.

items.name: Big White Opening Day 2026/27
items.text: the planned start of the winter season. Opening depends on snow conditions, so check the resort's latest news before you drive up.

items.name: SilverStar Alpine Opening Day 2026
items.text: the first day of lift-served skiing and snowboarding on the mountain.

items.name: Sovereign Canada Cup Cross-Country Ski Races
items.text: Canada's top cross-country skiers open the domestic race season at Sovereign Lake Nordic Centre. It's free to watch from the trailside.

items.name: Discover Okanagan Tours
items.text: a Kelowna operator that runs private ski shuttles in winter, as well as guided wine tours with pickup around town.

items.tip: many wineries, patios and seasonal attractions cut back from November to April. Check each listing's hours, and call ahead if a stop matters.
November is cool, often grey in the valley and colder up the hills. A warm jacket, a rain layer and good shoes cover most days.
the days are short, so put outdoor stops and winery visits early in the day.
roads to the ski hills can be snowy in late November. Drive with winter-ready tires and check road conditions before you go.
